subject: MAP: Performance benchmarking & final close timeline for Helix Health
messages:
From: Sarah Hall <sarah@helixhealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: kickoff - MAP / performance plan

Hi Dylan / Priyom —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Helix is excited to move the pilot toward production, and procurement asked me to get a concrete MAP that includes performance gating (latency, throughput, TTFT) before we sign. Our clinical workload is bursty during morning ingest windows and we need guidance on concurrency profiles.

Can you send a proposed evaluation plan that maps Redwood model variants to our success criteria, plus an estimate of time to close if everything looks good? Procurement will need a timeline for contract review (they asked for ~2 weeks) and I want the engineering team to align on test windows.

Key constraints:
- 95th pct latency target: <= 350 ms for the 4k-token median prompt mix
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) should be <= 120 ms for warm requests
- Sustained throughput target during ingest windows: 800 requests/min with 8 concurrent streams
- Data residency: US only

Appreciate a short MAP with milestones and a perf plan we can run in our environment.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Hall
Platform Eng, Helix Health
[Attachment: helix_requirements_summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Hall <sarah@helixhealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: kickoff - MAP / performance plan

Sarah —

Thanks for the note and the clear SLAs. We can put together a short MAP that ties evaluation milestones to the contract timeline. High-level plan below; I'll attach a draft benchmarking workbook and a variant comparison PDF for your team to review.

Summary (proposal):
- Week 0 (Aug 20-21): Validation run in Redwood hosted sandbox — smoke checks for integration and basic latency profile (team: Redwood SE + Helix devs).
- Week 1 (Aug 24-28): Detailed perf run using Helix representative traffic (4k median prompt mix). Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, sustained throughput, model quality on Helix prompts (auto eval + spot human checks).
- Week 2 (Aug 31-Sep 4): Variant gating and canary rollout plan. We’ll compare three variants: 1) rdx-large-fp16 (baseline quality, higher perf), 2) rdx-large-quant (4-bit quantized, higher throughput/lower cost), 3) rdx-1024-medium (smaller, best for low-latency interactive flows).
- Contract: Procurement review (2 weeks) runs parallel to the Week 1 perf run; if gating passes, we target signature by Sep 10 and go-live pilot in the following week.

Performance targets & gating criteria (proposal):
- Latency gating: p95 <= 350 ms (4k median prompt mix) on the production variant. Failure -> fallback to next compatible variant and re-run with caching tweaks.
- TTFT gating: <= 120 ms for warm requests; cold start analysis included but not gating unless > 300 ms.
- Throughput gating: sustained >= 800 req/min with 8 concurrent streams for 30 minutes. Spikes tolerated up to 1200 req/min for 5 minutes.
- Quality gating: automated BLEU/ROUGE style metrics + 100-sample human spot check (Helix labels) with no more than 5% regressions vs baseline acceptance prompts.

Attachments included: helix_map_benchmark_v1.xlsx (workbook with test harness and sample prompts), redwood_variant_report.pdf (variant perf/quality summary).

Next steps:
1) Priyom will share the test harness commands and a short script to replay Helix traffic.
2) Helix confirms the 2-week procurement window and whether Tom from procurement should be looped in now.
3) We’ll schedule a 1-hour lab run kickoff on Aug 24 (propose 10am PT).

I’ll drop the workbook into the Drive link and add acceptance criteria to the MAP doc for signatures.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: helix_map_benchmark_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Hall <sarah@helixhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: kickoff - MAP / performance plan

Sarah / Dylan —

Quick tech notes on running the benchmark at Helix:
- Test harness: use the provided helm chart and the run_bench.sh script in the workbook. The script supports: warm runs (preload KV cache), cold runs, and concurrency ramps.
- KV cache sizing: for your median 4k prompt mix we recommend prewarming with 25k tokens of typical prefixes to exercise cache hit ratios similar to production.
- Batch sizing: start with batch=8 for rdx-large-fp16 and batch=16 for rdx-large-quant — we’ll tune to hit p95 target.
- Canary config: set routing policy to prefer rdx-large-quant for cost-sensitive request types and rdx-large-fp16 for high-quality routes. Fallback order: rdx-large-fp16 -> rdx-large-quant -> rdx-1024-medium.

Model variant expected tradeoffs (short):
- rdx-large-fp16: highest quality, p95 latency ~320 ms at 8 concurrent streams (on dedicated instance profile we recommended). Cost: high.
- rdx-large-quant (4-bit): quality manager reports ~1-2% drop on hallucination-sensitive prompts; p95 latency expected ~260 ms, throughput up ~1.8x, cost ~40% lower. Good fit if Helix accepts small quality delta on batch ingestion flows.
- rdx-1024-medium: fastest tail latency (~180-220 ms p95), best for low-latency interactive; lower quality on long-context reasoning.

I’ll attach the quick commands to the Drive doc and the microbenchmark script. We can run a focused 90-minute perf lab with your infra team and produce numerical p50/p95/p99 + TTFT graphs.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_variant_report.pdf (pdf)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Hall <sarah@helixhealth.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-08-20T16:32:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & close cadence: proposed milestones and sign-offs

Hi Sarah / Tom / team —

Adding the commercial milestones to Dylan’s technical MAP so procurement has a clear view. Proposed mutual action plan and timeline (holistic):

Milestones:
1) Aug 24: Lab kickoff (1-hr) — smoke perf run and integration sign-off (owner: Redwood SE + Helix infra).
2) Aug 25–28: Helix ingestion perf runs (owner: Helix eng). Redwood provides scripts + on-call SE. Deliverable: p50/p95/p99, TTFT graphs, throughput stability report.
3) Aug 31–Sep 4: Variant gating and canary plan refinement (owner: Redwood + Helix). Deliverable: variant selection for pilot and rollback strategy document.
4) Sep 7: Legal/Procurement final redlines (owner: Helix procurement + Redwood GTM).
5) Sep 10: Signature target (if gating passes).
6) Sep 14: Pilot go-live (limited traffic) — 2-week pilot, then evaluate for full rollout.

Acceptance criteria to close deal (both technical & commercial):
- Technical acceptance: p95 <= 350 ms and TTFT <= 120 ms on agreed pilot variant for two 1-hour sustain windows during ingest; quality regressions <= 5% in spot-check.
- Commercial acceptance: final SOW and order form signed, data residency & SOC 2 clauses validated.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: quantized variant shows >5% quality regression on clinical prompts. Mitigation: default to fp16 for clinical route and use quantized for batch ingestion; Redwood will provide immediate fallback routing.
- Risk: short procurement timeline. Mitigation: we will freeze commercial terms for 5 business days after handing redlines to speed signature.

Please confirm: 1) Helix confirms procurement will target Sep 7 for final redlines, 2) Tom confirms he’s ok being in thread for procurement questions, and 3) Helix accepts the proposed week-of Aug 24 lab dates.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick alignment call tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan_helix.docx (docx)]

Thanks everyone — this looks good and aligns with our internal expectations. Quick confirmations:
- Procurement (Tom) confirmed target for Sep 7 redlines and is ok to be copied on the thread.
- We’re good for Aug 24 lab kickoff at 10am PT — Tom, please join if you can.
- Helix will run the Week 1 perf window Aug 25–28; we’ll share the traffic replay file by EOD Monday.

On variant preferences: engineering likes the idea of using rdx-large-quant for batch ingestion if the quality drop is confirmed <=2% in the lab. For clinical inference, we’ll keep fp16 by default. Please show the fallback routing in the canary doc during the lab.

We’ll accept the MAP with the acceptance criteria you listed — please push the final MAP doc to the Drive link and we’ll add signatures after the Week 1 perf run if gating passes.

See you on Aug 24.

Sarah
